title: POC capacity scenario triage & GPU economics — workshop notes
body:
Background:

Quick notes from the 2025-01-14 solution workshop run for a prospective enterprise customer (code-name: Silverline Health). Customer wants a Dedicated capacity POC to prove predictable latency for mixed workloads (chat + summarization + embeddings) with regulatory data residency requirements. Goal: produce 3 capacity scenarios (costed) and recommend autoscale policies that hit a 200ms median generation latency SLO for chat while keeping monthly GPU spend < $60k for baseline traffic.

Customer workload summary (collected from intake):
- Primary features: interactive chat (stateful, KV cache heavy), batched embedding pipelines (offline nightly), light reranking requests (low QPS but high token count).
- Expected steady QPS: 35 chat requests/sec average during work hours (09:00–18:00 local), 5 req/sec off-hours.
- Peak behaviour: scheduled marketing events produce 6x baseline for 30–90 minute windows, unpredictable small bursts from federated clients.
- Typical prompt length: 80–350 tokens. Response length target ~150 tokens.
- Latency target: median <= 200ms for chat (end-to-end generation for interactive path).

Workload characterization & risk notes:
- Chat workload benefits heavily from KV/prefix caching because many requests reuse system/prompt prefixes and short contexts.
- Embeddings are tolerant of batch latency (can be 5–30s) and should be routed to cheaper, high-throughput instances or scheduled off-peak.
- Reranking can be routed to quantized model variants with slightly degraded accuracy.
- Regulatory note: Private deployment required for full production; POC can run in Dedicated with restricted storage to satisfy data residency.

Sizing assumptions (micro-benchmarks we ran during workshop):
- Model variants tested: Llama-2-based 70B (fp16), 8-bit quantized 70B (q8), optimized 13B (fp16).
- Observed single-GPU steady throughputs (median tokens/sec, generation-only):
  - H100 80GB (fp16, 70B): 420 tokens/sec generation
  - A100 80GB (fp16, 70B): 330 tokens/sec generation
  - H100 (q8 70B): 560 tokens/sec generation (lower memory pressure enabled larger batch sizes)
  - L4-like 32GB for 13B (fp16): 1200 tokens/sec generation
- Tail latency multiplier for small-batch interactive (<4 tokens batched): ~1.6x vs large-batch perf. Cold-start penalty when evicting KV cache: +120ms median per request if cache miss occurs.

Three capacity scenarios (costed, simplified monthly)

Scenario A — Cost-conservative baseline (recommended POC start)
- Target: satisfy steady traffic with headroom for small bursts (x1.5). Use mixed pool: 2x H100 (reserved) + 1x L4-style nodes for routing small cheap model for non-sensitive embeddings & light tasks.
- Autoscale policy: manual reserve 2 H100, scheduled scale-up to 3 H100 for known event windows, reactive scale by +1 on CPU/GPU utilization > 75% for >4min with cooldown 6min. Pre-warm step before event windows (pre-warm KV cache via synthetic warmers).
- Estimated monthly cost (VM/GPU + infra + egress amortized): $44,000 — assumptions: H100 $8.4/hr reserved equivalent, L4 nodes $1.5/hr. Includes 20% buffer for storage/ops/overhead.
- Pros: predictable cost, simple policy, minimal ops complexity.
- Cons: may not fully absorb large unplanned bursts; median latency target likely met for steady traffic but tail spikes during sudden 6x events.

Scenario B — Performance-first with burst credits
- Target: meet median and p95 SLOs even during short bursts. Use 3x H100 reserved + 4x preemptible H100 for burst; aggressive autoscaling to add preemptible nodes when queue length > 20 requests or GPU utilization > 85%. Predictive scheduler uses short-term forecast (15min EWMA) from request traces to proactively add preemptible capacity.
- Autoscale tuning: scale-up step size = +2 GPUs (to avoid slow increments), cooldown 3min, aggressive pre-warm of KV cache (run replay of recent requests). Fallback model variant: switch to q8 70B on preemptible nodes during extreme load for cost saving and higher throughput.
- Estimated monthly cost: $58,000 (includes preemptible churn).
- Pros: strong latency guarantees, handles most bursts without degradation.
- Cons: higher cost and added complexity for preemptible handling and stateful routing.

Scenario C — Cost-optimized aggressive quantization
- Target: minimize spend while maintaining acceptable UX. Use 3x A100 (or mix A100 + L4) running quantized 70B (q8) for main traffic; offline embeddings run on cheaper CPU + GPU spot fleet. Autoscale conservatively: only add reserved nodes when sustained > 10min above threshold; rely on model variant fallback to smaller 13B for long-form outputs.
- Estimated monthly cost: $32,000.
- Pros: lowest cost.
- Cons: risk of quality regressions; tail latency may increase; heavier monitoring/evals required.

Autoscaling policy templates (examples to try during POC):
1) Scheduled + reactive hybrid (recommended first pass)
   - Scheduled windows: scale to N+1 for planned events (30–120min pre-window warmup).
   - Reactive trigger: GPU util > 70% sustained 3min OR request queue length > 15 for 2min -> add +1 GPU. Cooldown 6min.
   - Pre-warm: synthetic traffic replay of last 1,000 requests spread across 90s once scale completes.

2) Predictive (short-horizon forecasting)
   - Use 15-min EWMA and event calendar to request scale actions with a 5–15min lead time.
   - Maintain small reserve of preemptible GPUs for last-mile spikes.

3) Failover / graceful degradation policy
   - If scaling lag > 8min and queue depth > 60: route new requests to smaller model variant (13B fp16) and mark for async reprocess if required.
   - For privacy-sensitive requests, fallback to regional Dedicated pool or return soft fail with 503 + recommended retry.

Operational runbook snippets (POC-focused):
- Pre-POC: set up synthetic traffic generator with recorded sample from customer; prepare scripts to seed KV cache; define monitoring dashboards (per-route latency, per-GPU util, queue depth, token throughput).
- During POC: live tweak autoscale thresholds in small increments; run two controlled spike tests (3x and 6x) and capture traces; validate cold-start behavior after 30min idle.
- Post-POC: provide cost-reconciliation report and recommended production sizing (reserve vs dedicated ratio).

Open questions / decisions needed from customer:
- Tolerance for quantized models in production vs regulator-required cert matrix.
- Acceptable monthly budget range (is $60k a hard cap?).
- Will they accept preemptible capacity for bursts? Any restrictions on ephemeral compute?
- Event calendar accuracy: can they provide scheduled event times at least 24 hours in advance?

Immediate next steps / action items (owners):
- SE: prepare two runnable POC templates (A baseline + B performance-first) with terraform + kube manifests — due 2025-01-21 (Marcus Ruiz).
- Applied ML: produce a short evaluation plan for q8 vs fp16 quality delta on customer prompt set — due 2025-01-20 (Priya Nair).
- SRE/Infra: pre-provision a preemptible H100 pool and test preemption handling logic in routing layer — due 2025-01-24 (Liam O'Connor).
- Solutions Eng / Customer: schedule controlled spike tests with customer for 2025-01-28 and provide synthetic generator seed — due 2025-01-22 (Ava Chen).

Notes & heuristics used (for future reuse):
- When mixing instance types, route short-interaction chat to GPUs with lowest p95 latency (H100), route heavy batched jobs to cheaper quantized instances.
- Use token-based throughput estimates to convert QPS to GPU counts: estimated tokens/sec per GPU * SLO-informed latency headroom -> required GPUs. Always apply 20–30% safety headroom for tail variance unless using predictive autoscaling + warm cache.

Appendix (quick numbers snapshot):
- Cost units assumed in calculations: H100 equiv reserved $8.4/hr, H100 preemptible $3.1/hr, A100 equiv $6.2/hr, L4-class $1.5/hr.
- Example conversion: 35 chat req/s * 150 tokens/resp = 5250 tokens/sec -> with H100 fp16 @420 tokens/sec -> baseline GPUs = ceil(5250 / 420) = 13 -> but KV caching and batching expected to reduce effective tokens/sec load by ~6x for interactive paths -> effective GPUs required ~3.

End of notes.

Document history: draft created 2025-01-14 after workshop. Iterations ongoing with customer input.
